title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 144 (Guarantee on contract that creditor shall not act on it until co-surety joins)

content.overview: Section 144 provides that where a person gives a guarantee upon a contract that the creditor shall not act upon it until another person has joined in it as co-surety, the guarantee is not valid if that other person does not join.
content.glance: A guarantee given on the condition that a co-surety will join is not valid if that co-surety does not join.
content.study: Where a person gives a guarantee upon a contract that the creditor shall not act upon it until another person has joined in it as co-surety, the guarantee is not valid if that other person does not join. Current-law framing: the condition precedent of co-surety joining must be fulfilled.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: Where a person gives a guarantee upon a contract that the creditor shall not act upon it until another person has joined in it as co-surety, the guarantee is not valid if that other person does not join.

examples.title: Conditional co-surety
examples.body: Surety gives guarantee on condition that another joins as co-surety. If the other does not join, the guarantee is not valid under Section 144.

hypotheticals.question: A guarantees on the express condition that B will also join as co-surety. B never joins. Is A's guarantee valid?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 144 provides that the guarantee is not valid if the other person does not join.
